sections.title: The letters -stle
paragraphs: The letters -stle sound like /səl/. You hear this ending in (castle) /kɑː.səl/, which means a large stone fort. This letter group makes one sound pattern. It ends with a light hiss and a quick closing consonant. The middle letter stays quiet every time.

sections.title: How to say -stle
paragraphs: Put your tongue tip near the ridge behind your upper teeth. Push air out to make a smooth hiss. Do not turn your voice on. Next, lift your tongue tip against the ridge. Turn your voice on and let air escape along the sides of your tongue. Put your fingers on your throat to feel the voice start only on the second part.

sections.title: Spelling of -stle
paragraphs: The letters -stle appear at the end of a word. A silent letter is a letter that you write but do not say. The t is always a silent letter in this ending. Say the group as /səl/ in (castle) /kɑː.səl/. You also hear this same pattern in (rustle) /rʌ.səl/.

sections.title: Common mistakes with -stle
paragraphs: Many learners try to say every letter and add a t sound. Do not pop your tongue down to make a burst of air. Say the ending smoothly as a hiss followed by an l. Glide straight from the hiss into the final consonant. Keep your voice off during the hiss.
